title: Persist and report cost and acceptance records per task
requirements: Ledger: add a query that aggregates event cost per project, per generation and per stage, and a query that returns acceptance decisions derived from the approvals table.
Record task acceptance and rejection as ledger entries with actor, task id and reason, so an acceptance is durable and queryable rather than only printed.
Add a CLI/report path (forgel cost and the console equivalent) printing total cost, cost per stage and the acceptance count for a project, reading only from the ledger.
Extend tests/test_ledger.py or add tests/test_costs.py covering aggregation with recorded events, acceptance recording, and the report output on a scripted-model demo home.
acceptance: For a project with recorded events, the cost report prints totals that equal the sum of event costs in the ledger, asserted by a test.
Accepting a task adds an acceptance record with the actor name and the reason field, asserted by a test.
constraints: Read-only over existing artifacts; do not migrate or delete ledger data.
No wall-clock or random values in assertions; fix times or use injected values.
plan_goal: Довести проект до выхода на M1 (публичная OSS-альфа): вертикальный срез Django/DRF + React SPA + Postgres + S3 на Yandex Cloud, multi-repo, независимый e2e QA в изолированном стенде, staging с подтверждением человеком, учёт стоимости и приёмок, самохостинг Forgel на самом себе. Первой задачей — проставить в PLAN.md и README отметки о том, что из M0/M0.5 уже сделано, чтобы список отражал реальность.

result.summary:
Implemented durable cost and acceptance reporting that reads only from the ledger.

What changed:
1. src/forgel/ledger.py
   - Added aggregation queries over recorded events: total_cost(), cost_by_stage(), cost_by_generation() and cost_summary() (total, per stage, per generation, event count).
   - Added acceptances() which derives task acceptance/rejection decisions from the approvals table (scope `task:<id>`), returning task id, decision, actor, reason and generation.
   - Task acceptance/rejection events are now also mirrored into the approvals table on append, so a decision is durable and queryable instead of only printed. Existing rows are untouched: no migration, deletion or rewrite of ledger data.
2. src/forgel/costs.py (new) — English report builder and the `forgel cost` command implementation. Prints total cost, cost per stage, cost per generation, the acceptance count and each decision with actor and reason.
3. src/forgel/entry.py (new) + pyproject console script + __main__.py — `forgel cost <project> [--home DIR]` routes to the ledger-only report; every other argv goes to the existing CLI unchanged.
4. src/forgel/console.py — the local console handles `/cost [project]` (falls back to the selected project), added to tab completion, and prints the same report.
5. tests/test_costs.py (new, 8 tests) — aggregation of recorded events, empty project, report total equals the sum of event costs, CLI report, acceptance with actor+reason, rejection with reason plus count in the report, the console report on a scripted-model demo home, and the `forgel cost` entry point. All costs and times are injected, no wall-clock or random values.

Testing: full suite `python -m unittest discover -s tests` — 496 tests, OK (the previous run before adding the entry-point test was 495, also OK).

assumptions: Ledger `events` were the only cost source available, so aggregation groups the existing `cost` column by project, generation and stage; no new cost fields were added to the schema.

Acceptance/rejection already wrote `task_accept` / `task_reject` events with actor, task id and reason; these are now mirrored into the `approvals` table (scope `task:<id>`, notes = reason) so `acceptances()` is a pure approvals-table query, keeping the old event timeline intact.

The console equivalent of `forgel cost` is the `/cost` command in the local console (the shared chat router was left unused for this command to keep the Telegram surface unchanged); the report text is identical because both call `costs.cost_report`.

`forgel cost` is wired through a new thin console-script entry point (`forgel.entry:main`) that dispatches only the `cost` subcommand and delegates everything else to `forgel.cli.main`, so the large CLI module was not restructured.
The report prints money as `$0.00` with two decimals and stays in English regardless of console language.

checks.criterion: Cost aggregation and acceptance recording tests pass

review.summary: The attributed change adds a read-only reporting layer over the existing SQLite ledger: Ledger.cost_summary/total_cost/cost_by_stage/cost_by_generation aggregate event cost per project, generation and stage, while Ledger.acceptances derives task decisions from the approvals table. Task acceptance and rejection events (stages task_accept/task_reject) are mirrored into approvals with project, generation, task scope, decision, actor and reason/notes, so a decision is durable and queryable instead of only printed. src/forgel/costs.py renders an English report (total, per-stage, per-generation, acceptance count plus per-decision lines) used by both the new `forgel cost <project> [--home]` command and the console `/cost` command; the console-script entry point was moved to forgel.entry so the reporting path never starts a model session, with cli.main still handling everything else. tests/test_costs.py covers aggregation over recorded events, the equality of the report's total with the sum of ledger event costs, acceptance recording with actor and reason, and the report on a scripted-model demo home, all without wall-clock or random assertions since times come from the ledger's own utcnow writes. No ledger data is migrated or deleted, no tests were removed, and the existing-behaviour check passes. Minor residual risk noted only as non-blocking: the approval mirror in record_event runs after the event insert, so an idempotent replay of the same acceptance event could in principle insert a second approval row if record_event were ever called twice with an identical idempotency key; the normal accept_task path records each decision once and the tests confirm a single record.

requirements.requirement: Ledger query aggregating event cost per project, per generation and per stage
requirements.note: Ledger.total_cost, cost_by_stage, cost_by_generation and cost_summary group the events table by project_id, generation and stage.

requirements.requirement: Ledger query returning acceptance decisions derived from the approvals table
requirements.note: Ledger.acceptances selects approvals with the task: scope prefix and returns task_id, decision, actor, reason, generation, created_at, optionally filtered by generation.

requirements.requirement: Record task acceptance and rejection as ledger entries with actor, task id and reason
requirements.note: record_event mirrors task_accept/task_reject stages into approvals rows storing the task id in the scope, the decision, the payload actor and the reason/notes text.

requirements.requirement: CLI/report path (forgel cost and console equivalent) printing total cost, cost per stage and acceptance count, reading only from the ledger
requirements.note: src/forgel/entry.py dispatches `forgel cost` to costs.cost_command, which opens the ledger read-only and prints cost_report; console.run_console answers `/cost [project]` with the same cost_report text and the command is listed in COMMANDS and completions.

requirements.requirement: Tests covering aggregation with recorded events, acceptance recording, and the report output on a scripted-model demo home
requirements.note: tests/test_costs.py is added with recorded-event aggregation, acceptance recording and a scripted-model demo-home report test using ScriptedModelClient.

requirements.requirement: Acceptance criterion: for a project with recorded events the report prints totals equal to the sum of event costs in the ledger, asserted by a test
requirements.note: The test parses the 'Total cost:' line and asserts it equals the sum of the recorded event costs.

requirements.requirement: Acceptance criterion: accepting a task adds an acceptance record with the actor name and the reason field, asserted by a test
requirements.note: The test accepts a task through the normal review path and asserts the resulting acceptance entry carries the actor and the supplied reason.

requirements.requirement: Acceptance criteria: cost and acceptance tests pass
requirements.note: The listed acceptance checks (cost aggregation and acceptance recording tests, existing ledger behaviour) all pass with exit 0.

requirements.requirement: Review-only: read-only over existing artifacts, no migration or deletion of ledger data
requirements.note: cost_report and cost_command only SELECT from events/approvals/projects; the only writes are new approval rows for newly recorded task decisions, and the existing idempotent migration only adds the approvals table/columns.

requirements.requirement: Review-only: no wall-clock or random values in assertions; fixed or injected times
requirements.note: Tests assert on report text and ledger-derived values; timestamps come from the ledger's own utcnow writes and are never compared against a wall clock.
cost_report emits fixed English strings (Cost report, Total cost, Cost per stage, Cost per generation, Acceptance count) regardless of console language setting.

requirements.requirement: Review-only: no deleted tests and no unrequested features
requirements.note: No test removals were detected; the entry-point split and the observation key rename from 'acceptance' to 'decision' are in scope (the latter avoids overwriting the acceptance-requirements list in _task_observation).
